_about: Scoring template: the rubric and calculation rules evaluate_world.py uses. Copy it to another project and change the values, not the code. A world can override it with its own scoring.json at the world root. The method is described in references/scoring.md.
bands: good: usable, fix the listed issues
fair: fix the issues before making stories

status._about: Colour coding. Scores 0-100: pass (green) at or above pass, check (amber) at or above check, else fail (red). Quality criteria 1-5 use criterion. Breadth parts: pass at full marks, check at or above the minimum, fail below it. Checklist areas: pass when every item is done, else fail. Approvals: pass when all are approved, else check.

quality._about: Each criterion is scored 1-5 by the reviewer (1 = fails, 3 = usable with visible flaws, 5 = no flaw found). Quality = sum(weight x (score - 1) / 4) / sum(weight) x 100, only when every criterion is scored.

criteria.label: Character identity
criteria.means_5: Each character looks the same on its sheet, in every group picture and on the height chart: face, hair or fur, eyes, colours, outfit.

criteria.label: Pictures match the canon
criteria.means_5: Sheets, sets and props agree with the text of Identities.md and Setting.md (hair, clothes, colours, eye size, furniture); where they differ, the canon was changed to match.

criteria.label: True sizes
criteria.means_5: Relative sizes follow height_cm in every picture; the height chart is to scale.

criteria.label: Group pictures keep the sets
criteria.means_5: Group scenes keep their location's camera view, layout and furniture; nothing invented, moved or missing.

criteria.label: One art style
criteria.means_5: Sheets, sets, props and group pictures share one rendering style and light.

criteria.label: Clean pictures
criteria.means_5: No text, logos, watermarks, borders, extra people or animals, or generation artefacts (hands, eyes, melted objects).

criteria.label: Voices
criteria.means_5: Each voice fits its character, follows the language and accent rules, speaks every line correctly (see the transcripts) at the agreed pace; the dialogue sounds like one conversation.

breadth._about: Part score = min(count, full) / full x 100. Breadth = sum(weight x part score) / sum(weight). A count below its minimum is also a missing checklist item. "per_location" means one per location: minimum and full marks are the number of locations.

checklist._about: Not scored. Completeness = items done / items checked x 100. Every item is needed before stories.
